newsitem.title: CANADA: Concorde, with rock legends on board, forced to land.
newsitem.headline: Concorde, with rock legends on board, forced to land.

text.p: A British Airways Concorde jet on which British rock legends Elton John and Pete Townshend were passengers made an emergency landing in Halifax, Nova Scotia on Friday.
The supersonic jet, en route to New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport from London, detoured to Halifax after it developed engine trouble over the Atlantic, airline officials said.
The plane landed safely in the Canadian east coast city shortly before 10 a.m. (1500 GMT) on three of its four engines.
"The captain experienced a problem with number three engine and purely as a precautionary measure, he decided to divert to Halifax," British Airways spokeswoman Honour Verrier said.
She was unable to provide details on the nature of the engine problem. The jet landed without incident and no passengers were injured.
The Concorde passengers, including John and Townshend, were taken to New York later on Friday afternoon on a British Airways Boeing 747, Farmer said.
